237: static struct wifi_command_slot *wifi_command_alloc(void)
238: {
239:   unsigned int i;
240: 
241:   for (i = 0; i < BK7258_WIFI_CMD_SLOTS; i++)
242:     {
243:       uint32_t *pattern = (uint32_t *)g_wifi.command[i].bytes;
244: 
245:       if (!g_wifi.command[i].owned &&
246:           !g_wifi.command[i].transport_pending &&
247:           *pattern == BK7258_WIFI_CMD_PATTERN_FREE)
248:         {
249:           g_wifi.command[i].owned = true;
250:           *pattern = BK7258_WIFI_CMD_PATTERN_BUSY;
251:           return &g_wifi.command[i];
252:         }
253:     }
254: 
255:   return NULL;
256: }

258: static void wifi_command_reap(void)
259: {
260:   unsigned int i;
261: 
262:   for (i = 0; i < BK7258_WIFI_CMD_SLOTS; i++)
263:     {
264:       uint32_t pattern = *(uint32_t *)g_wifi.command[i].bytes;
265: 
266:       if (g_wifi.command[i].owned &&
267:           !g_wifi.command[i].transport_pending &&
268:           pattern == BK7258_WIFI_CMD_PATTERN_FREE)
269:         {
270:           g_wifi.command[i].owned = false;
271:         }
272:     }
273: }

275: static void wifi_command_transport_complete(
276:   const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *ack, int result, void *arg)
277: {
278:   struct wifi_command_slot *slot = arg;
279:   bool wake = false;
280:   irqstate_t flags;
281: 
282:   (void)ack;
283:   flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
284:   if (slot->transport_pending)
285:     {
286:       slot->transport_pending = false;
287:       if (result == -EREMOTEIO && slot->owned)
288:         {
289:           *(uint32_t *)slot->bytes = BK7258_WIFI_CMD_PATTERN_FREE;
290:           slot->owned = false;
291:           if (g_wifi.waiting_id ==
292:                 slot->command + BK7258_WIFI_CFM_OFFSET &&
293:               g_wifi.waiting_sequence == slot->sequence)
294:             {
295:               g_wifi.command_result = -EREMOTEIO;
296:               g_wifi.waiting_id = 0;
297:               wake = true;
298:             }
299:         }
300:     }
301:   rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
302: 
303:   if (wake)
304:     {
305:       nxsem_post(&g_wifi.command_sem);
306:     }
307: }

309: static int wifi_command(uint16_t command, const void *payload,
310:                          uint16_t payload_length, void *result,
311:                          uint16_t result_size, uint16_t *result_length)
312: {
313:   struct wifi_command_slot *slot;
314:   struct bk7258_wifi_cpdu *cpdu;
315:   struct bk7258_wifi_msg_hdr *header;
316:   uint16_t sequence;
317:   int ret;
318: 
319:   if (payload_length > BK7258_WIFI_CMD_SLOT_SIZE - sizeof(uint32_t) -
320:                        sizeof(*cpdu) - sizeof(*header))
321:     {
322:       return -E2BIG;
323:     }
324: 
325:   if (!bk7258_mailbox_link_ready())
326:     {
327:       return -ENOLINK;
328:     }
329: 
330:   nxmutex_lock(&g_wifi.command_lock);
331:   nxmutex_lock(&g_wifi.packet_lock);
332:   wifi_command_reap();
333:   slot = wifi_command_alloc();
334:   if (slot == NULL)
335:     {
336:       nxmutex_unlock(&g_wifi.packet_lock);
337:       nxmutex_unlock(&g_wifi.command_lock);
338:       return -ENOMEM;
339:     }
340: 
341:   cpdu = (struct bk7258_wifi_cpdu *)(slot->bytes + sizeof(uint32_t));
342:   header = (struct bk7258_wifi_msg_hdr *)(cpdu + 1);
343:   sequence = ++g_wifi.next_sequence;
344:   memset(cpdu, 0, sizeof(*cpdu) + sizeof(*header) + payload_length);
345:   cpdu->length = sizeof(*cpdu) + sizeof(*header) + payload_length;
346:   header->cmd_id = command;
347:   header->cmd_sn = sequence;
348:   header->length = payload_length;
349:   slot->command = command;
350:   slot->sequence = sequence;
351:   slot->generation = bk7258_mailbox_peer_reset_generation();
352:   slot->transport_pending = true;
353:   if (payload != NULL && payload_length != 0)
354:     {
355:       memcpy(header + 1, payload, payload_length);
356:     }
357: 
358:   while (nxsem_trywait(&g_wifi.command_sem) == OK)
359:     {
360:     }
361: 
362:   {
363:     irqstate_t flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
364: 
365:     g_wifi.waiting_id = command + BK7258_WIFI_CFM_OFFSET;
366:     g_wifi.waiting_sequence = sequence;
367:     g_wifi.command_result = -ETIMEDOUT;
368:     g_wifi.command_length = 0;
369:     rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
370:   }
371:   ret = wifi_send_node(BK7258_WIFI_CMD_TX_CHANNEL, 0,
372:                        (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)cpdu,
373:                        (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)cpdu, 1,
374:                        wifi_command_transport_complete, slot);
375:   if (ret < 0)
376:     {
377:       *(uint32_t *)slot->bytes = BK7258_WIFI_CMD_PATTERN_FREE;
378:       slot->owned = false;
379:       slot->transport_pending = false;
380:       {
381:         irqstate_t flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
382: 
383:         if (g_wifi.waiting_id == command + BK7258_WIFI_CFM_OFFSET &&
384:             g_wifi.waiting_sequence == sequence)
385:           {
386:             g_wifi.waiting_id = 0;
387:           }
388:         rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
389:       }
390:       nxmutex_unlock(&g_wifi.packet_lock);
391:       nxmutex_unlock(&g_wifi.command_lock);
392:       return ret;
393:     }
394:   nxmutex_unlock(&g_wifi.packet_lock);
395: 
396:   ret = nxsem_tickwait_uninterruptible(&g_wifi.command_sem,
397:                                        WIFI_COMMAND_TIMEOUT);
398:   {
399:     irqstate_t flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
400: 
401:     if (g_wifi.waiting_id == command + BK7258_WIFI_CFM_OFFSET &&
402:         g_wifi.waiting_sequence == sequence)
403:       {
404:         g_wifi.waiting_id = 0;
405:       }
406:     if (ret >= 0)
407:       {
408:         ret = g_wifi.command_result;
409:       }
410:     rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
411:   }
412: 
413:   if (ret >= 0 && result != NULL && result_size != 0)
414:     {
415:       uint16_t copy = g_wifi.command_length < result_size ?
416:                       g_wifi.command_length : result_size;
417:       memcpy(result, g_wifi.command_data, copy);
418:     }
419:   if (ret >= 0 && result_length != NULL)
420:     {
421:       *result_length = g_wifi.command_length;
422:     }
423: 
424:   nxmutex_lock(&g_wifi.packet_lock);
425:   wifi_command_reap();
426:   nxmutex_unlock(&g_wifi.packet_lock);
427:   nxmutex_unlock(&g_wifi.command_lock);
428:   return ret;
429: }

570: static void wifi_sta_event(bool connected)
571: {
572:   bool carrier = false;
573:   bool handled = false;
574:   bool stopped = false;
575:   irqstate_t flags;
576: 
577:   nxmutex_lock(&g_wifi.packet_lock);
578:   flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
579:   if (g_wifi.active_role == WIFI_ROLE_STA)
580:     {
581:       handled = true;
582:       if (connected && g_wifi.role_state != WIFI_ROLE_STOPPING)
583:         {
584:           g_wifi.role_state = WIFI_ROLE_ACTIVE;
585:           g_wifi.tx_gate = g_wifi.admin_up;
586:           carrier = g_wifi.admin_up;
587:         }
588:       else if (!connected)
589:         {
590:           g_wifi.tx_gate = false;
591:           g_wifi.role_epoch++;
592:           g_wifi.packet_head = 0;
593:           g_wifi.packet_tail = 0;
594:           g_wifi.packet_count = 0;
595:           if (g_wifi.role_state == WIFI_ROLE_STOPPING)
596:             {
597:               g_wifi.active_role = WIFI_ROLE_NONE;
598:               g_wifi.role_state = WIFI_ROLE_IDLE;
599:               stopped = true;
600:             }
601:           else
602:             {
603:               /* CP auto-reconnect keeps the STA role alive after a transient
604:                * link loss.  The next connected event can restore carrier. */
605: 
606:               g_wifi.role_state = WIFI_ROLE_STARTING;
607:             }
608:         }
609:     }
610:   rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
611:   nxmutex_unlock(&g_wifi.packet_lock);
612:   if (stopped)
613:     {
614:       nxsem_post(&g_wifi.role_sem);
615:     }
616:   if (handled)
617:     {
618:       wifi_set_carrier(carrier);
619:     }
620: }

724: static bool wifi_sync_reset_generation(void)
725: {
726:   struct wifi_pending_node nodes[WIFI_NODE_QUEUE];
727:   uint32_t generation = bk7258_mailbox_peer_reset_generation();
728:   bool wake_command = false;
729:   unsigned int kept = 0;
730:   unsigned int i;
731:   irqstate_t flags;
732: 
733:   if (generation == g_wifi.reset_generation)
734:     {
735:       return false;
736:     }
737: 
738:   flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
739:   if (g_wifi.waiting_id != 0)
740:     {
741:       g_wifi.command_result = -ECONNRESET;
742:       g_wifi.waiting_id = 0;
743:       wake_command = true;
744:     }
745: 
746:   rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
747:   if (wake_command)
748:     {
749:       nxsem_post(&g_wifi.command_sem);
750:     }
751: 
752:   wifi_role_deactivate(WIFI_ROLE_NONE);
753:   nxmutex_lock(&g_wifi.scan_lock);
754:   wifi_scan_cache_clear();
755:   g_wifi.scan_running = false;
756:   nxmutex_unlock(&g_wifi.scan_lock);
757: 
758:   nxmutex_lock(&g_wifi.packet_lock);
759:   flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
760:   generation = bk7258_mailbox_peer_reset_generation();
761: 
762:   /* A peer generation change proves the old CP can no longer reference AP
763:    * command slots.  TX slots remain quarantined because DMA completion is
764:    * not proven by a CP reset.
765:    */
766: 
767:   for (i = 0; i < BK7258_WIFI_CMD_SLOTS; i++)
768:     {
769:       if (g_wifi.command[i].owned &&
770:           g_wifi.command[i].generation != generation)
771:         {
772:           *(uint32_t *)g_wifi.command[i].bytes =
773:             BK7258_WIFI_CMD_PATTERN_FREE;
774:           g_wifi.command[i].owned = false;
775:           g_wifi.command[i].transport_pending = false;
776:         }
777:     }
778:   g_wifi.reset_generation = generation;
779:   for (i = 0; i < g_wifi.node_count; i++)
780:     {
781:       unsigned int index = (g_wifi.node_head + i) % WIFI_NODE_QUEUE;
782: 
783:       if (g_wifi.nodes[index].generation == generation)
784:         {
785:           nodes[kept++] = g_wifi.nodes[index];
786:         }
787:     }
788:   memcpy(g_wifi.nodes, nodes, kept * sizeof(nodes[0]));
789:   g_wifi.node_head = 0;
790:   g_wifi.node_tail = kept % WIFI_NODE_QUEUE;
791:   g_wifi.node_count = kept;
792:   g_wifi.packet_head = 0;
793:   g_wifi.packet_tail = 0;
794:   g_wifi.packet_count = 0;
795:   for (i = 0; i < WIFI_RECYCLE_QUEUE; i++)
796:     {
797:       if (g_wifi.recycle[i].state != WIFI_RECYCLE_FREE &&
798:           g_wifi.recycle[i].generation != generation)
799:         {
800:           g_wifi.recycle[i].state = WIFI_RECYCLE_DISCARD;
801:         }
802:     }
803:   rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
804:   nxmutex_unlock(&g_wifi.packet_lock);
805:   nxsem_post(&g_wifi.work_sem);
806:   return true;
807: }

809: static int wifi_scan_cache_append(const void *data, size_t length)
810: {
811:   if (length > WIFI_SCAN_CACHE_LIMIT - g_wifi.scan_cache_length)
812:     {
813:       return -E2BIG;
814:     }
815: 
816:   memcpy(g_wifi.scan_cache + g_wifi.scan_cache_length, data, length);
817:   g_wifi.scan_cache_length += length;
818:   return OK;
819: }

821: static int wifi_scan_cache_event(uint16_t command, const void *data,
822:                                  size_t length)
823: {
824:   struct iw_event event;
825: 
826:   memset(&event, 0, sizeof(event));
827:   event.cmd = command;
828:   event.len = offsetof(struct iw_event, u) + length;
829:   if (length > sizeof(event.u))
830:     {
831:       return -E2BIG;
832:     }
833:   memcpy(&event.u, data, length);
834:   return wifi_scan_cache_append(&event, event.len);
835: }

837: static int wifi_scan_cache_build_record(
838:   const struct bk7258_wifi_scan_record *record)
839: {
840:   struct iw_event event;
841:   struct iw_quality quality;
842:   struct iw_freq frequency;
843:   uint16_t flags;
844:   size_t ssid_length;
845:   size_t padded_length;
846:   size_t event_length;
847:   int ret;
848: 
849:   memset(&event, 0, sizeof(event));
850:   event.cmd = SIOCGIWAP;
851:   event.len = IW_EV_LEN(ap_addr);
852:   event.u.ap_addr.sa_family = ARPHRD_ETHER;
853:   memcpy(event.u.ap_addr.sa_data, record->bssid, sizeof(record->bssid));
854:   ret = wifi_scan_cache_append(&event, event.len);
855:   if (ret < 0)
856:     {
857:       return ret;
858:     }
859: 
860:   ssid_length = strnlen(record->ssid, sizeof(record->ssid));
861:   padded_length = (ssid_length + 3u) & ~3u;
862:   memset(&event, 0, sizeof(event));
863:   event.cmd = SIOCGIWESSID;
864:   event.u.essid.flags = IW_ESSID_ON;
865:   event.u.essid.length = ssid_length;
866:   event.u.essid.pointer = (void *)(uintptr_t)sizeof(struct iw_point);
867:   event_length = offsetof(struct iw_event, u) + sizeof(struct iw_point) +
868:                  padded_length;
869:   event.len = event_length;
870:   ret = wifi_scan_cache_append(&event, offsetof(struct iw_event, u) +
871:                                sizeof(struct iw_point));
872:   if (ret < 0)
873:     {
874:       return ret;
875:     }
876:   ret = wifi_scan_cache_append(record->ssid, ssid_length);
877:   if (ret < 0)
878:     {
879:       return ret;
880:     }
881:   if (padded_length != ssid_length)
882:     {
883:       uint32_t padding = 0;
884:       ret = wifi_scan_cache_append(&padding, padded_length - ssid_length);
885:       if (ret < 0)
886:         {
887:           return ret;
888:         }
889:     }
890: 
891:   memset(&quality, 0, sizeof(quality));
892:   quality.level = (uint8_t)record->rssi;
893:   quality.updated = IW_QUAL_DBM;
894:   ret = wifi_scan_cache_event(IWEVQUAL, &quality, sizeof(quality));
895:   if (ret < 0)
896:     {
897:       return ret;
898:     }
899: 
900:   memset(&frequency, 0, sizeof(frequency));
901:   frequency.m = record->channel;
902:   ret = wifi_scan_cache_event(SIOCGIWFREQ, &frequency, sizeof(frequency));
903:   if (ret < 0)
904:     {
905:       return ret;
906:     }
907: 
908:   flags = record->security == 0 ? IW_ENCODE_DISABLED : IW_ENCODE_ENABLED;
909:   memset(&event, 0, sizeof(event));
910:   event.cmd = SIOCGIWENCODE;
911:   event.len = IW_EV_LEN(data);
912:   event.u.data.flags = flags;
913:   return wifi_scan_cache_append(&event, event.len);
914: }

916: static int wifi_scan_cache_fetch(void)
917: {
918:   struct bk7258_wifi_scan_page_request request;
919:   struct bk7258_wifi_scan_page_response response;
920:   uint16_t start = 0;
921:   uint16_t total = 0;
922:   uint16_t result_length;
923:   int ret;
924: 
925:   g_wifi.scan_cache = kmm_malloc(WIFI_SCAN_CACHE_LIMIT);
926:   if (g_wifi.scan_cache == NULL)
927:     {
928:       return -ENOMEM;
929:     }
930: 
931:   do
932:     {
933:       memset(&request, 0, sizeof(request));
934:       request.start = start;
935:       request.max_records = BK7258_WIFI_SCAN_PAGE_RECORDS;
936:       memset(&response, 0, sizeof(response));
937:       ret = wifi_command(BK7258_WIFI_CMD_OPENVELA_SCAN_PAGE,
938:                          &request, sizeof(request), &response,
939:                          sizeof(response), &result_length);
940:       if (ret < 0)
941:         {
942:           printf("wifi scan page transport failed: %d\n", ret);
943:           wifi_scan_cache_clear();
944:           return ret;
945:         }
946:       if (result_length != sizeof(response) || response.status != 0 ||
947:           response.page.start != start ||
948:           response.page.count > BK7258_WIFI_SCAN_PAGE_RECORDS ||
949:           response.page.reserved != 0 ||
950:           response.page.total < start ||
951:           response.page.count > response.page.total - start)
952:         {
953:           printf("wifi scan page invalid: status=%ld start=%u count=%u "
954:                  "total=%u length=%u\n",
955:                  (long)response.status, response.page.start,
956:                  response.page.count, response.page.total, result_length);
957:           wifi_scan_cache_clear();
958:           return response.status != 0 ? response.status : -EPROTO;
959:         }
960: 
961:       if (start == 0)
962:         {
963:           total = response.page.total;
964:         }
965:       else if (response.page.total != total)
966:         {
967:           wifi_scan_cache_clear();
968:           return -EPROTO;
969:         }
970: 
971:       for (uint8_t i = 0; i < response.page.count; i++)
972:         {
973:           ret = wifi_scan_cache_build_record(&response.page.records[i]);
974:           if (ret < 0)
975:             {
976:               wifi_scan_cache_clear();
977:               return ret;
978:             }
979:         }
980: 
981:       start += response.page.count;
982:       if (response.page.more != (start < total) ||
983:           (response.page.count == 0 && start < total))
984:         {
985:           wifi_scan_cache_clear();
986:           return -EPROTO;
987:         }
988:     }
989:   while (start < total);
990: 
991:   g_wifi.scan_cached = true;
992:   return OK;
993: }

995: static void wifi_release_cp_command(uint32_t cpdu_address)
996: {
997:   uint32_t pattern_address = cpdu_address - sizeof(uint32_t);

999:   if (wifi_cp_pointer(pattern_address, sizeof(uint32_t)))
1000:     {
1001:       *(uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)pattern_address =
1002:         BK7258_WIFI_CMD_PATTERN_FREE;
1003:       __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
1004:     }
1005: }

1007: static void wifi_handle_command(uint32_t cpdu_address,
1008:                                 uint32_t generation)
1009: {
1010:   struct bk7258_wifi_cpdu cpdu;
1011:   struct bk7258_wifi_event_hdr event;
1012:   uint8_t data[sizeof(g_wifi.command_data)];
1013:   uint32_t event_address;
1014:   uint16_t length;
1015:   uint16_t copied;
1016:   irqstate_t flags;
1017: 
1018:   flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
1019:   if (generation != bk7258_mailbox_peer_reset_generation() ||
1020:       !wifi_cp_pointer(cpdu_address, sizeof(cpdu)))
1021:     {
1022:       rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1023:       return;
1024:     }
1025: 
1026:   memcpy(&cpdu, (const void *)(uintptr_t)cpdu_address, sizeof(cpdu));
1027:   event_address = cpdu_address + sizeof(cpdu);
1028:   if (cpdu.length < sizeof(cpdu) + sizeof(event) ||
1029:       !wifi_cp_range(event_address, sizeof(event)))
1030:     {
1031:       rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1032:       return;
1033:     }
1034: 
1035:   memcpy(&event, (const void *)(uintptr_t)event_address, sizeof(event));
1036:   length = event.length;
1037:   if (length > cpdu.length - sizeof(cpdu) - sizeof(event) ||
1038:       !wifi_cp_range(event_address + WIFI_EVENT_DATA_OFFSET, length))
1039:     {
1040:       rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1041:       return;
1042:     }
1043: 
1044:   copied = length < sizeof(data) ? length : sizeof(data);
1045:   if (copied != 0)
1046:     {
1047:       memcpy(data, (const void *)(uintptr_t)(event_address +
1048:                                               WIFI_EVENT_DATA_OFFSET),
1049:              copied);
1050:     }
1051:   wifi_release_cp_command(cpdu_address);
1052:   rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1053: 
1054:   if (event.id >= BK7258_WIFI_CFM_OFFSET)
1055:     {
1056:       flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
1057: 
1058:       if (event.id == g_wifi.waiting_id &&
1059:           event.sequence == g_wifi.waiting_sequence)
1060:         {
1061:           if (copied != 0)
1062:             {
1063:               memcpy(g_wifi.command_data, data, copied);
1064:             }
1065:           g_wifi.command_length = copied;
1066:           g_wifi.command_result = OK;
1067:           g_wifi.waiting_id = 0;
1068:           rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1069:           nxsem_post(&g_wifi.command_sem);
1070:         }
1071:       else
1072:         {
1073:           rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1074:         }
1075:     }
1076:   else if (event.id == BK7258_WIFI_EVT_IPV4_IND)
1077:     {
1078:       wifi_sta_event(true);
1079:     }
1080:   else if (event.id == BK7258_WIFI_EVT_WIFI_EVENT_IND && copied >= 4)
1081:     {
1082:       uint16_t event_id;
1083: 
1084:       memcpy(&event_id, data, sizeof(event_id));
1085:       if (event_id == BK7258_WIFI_EVENT_CONNECTED)
1086:         {
1087:           wifi_sta_event(true);
1088:         }
1089:       else if (event_id == BK7258_WIFI_EVENT_DISCONNECTED)
1090:         {
1091:           wifi_sta_event(false);
1092:         }
1093:     }
1094:   else if (event.id == BK7258_WIFI_EVT_DISCONNECT_IND)
1095:     {
1096:       wifi_sta_event(false);
1097:     }
1098:   else if (event.id == BK7258_WIFI_EVT_START_AP_IND && copied >= 1)
1099:     {
1100:       wifi_ap_start_event(data[0] == 0);
1101:     }
1102:   else if (event.id == BK7258_WIFI_EVT_ASSOC_AP_IND && copied >= 6)
1103:     {
1104:       wifi_ap_client_event(true);
1105:     }
1106:   else if (event.id == BK7258_WIFI_EVT_DISASSOC_AP_IND && copied >= 6)
1107:     {
1108:       wifi_ap_client_event(false);
1109:     }
1110:   else if (event.id == BK7258_WIFI_EVT_STOP_AP_IND)
1111:     {

1115:     {

1121: static bool wifi_validate_command(uint32_t cpdu_address,
1122:                                   uint32_t *next, uint32_t generation)
1123: {
1124:   struct bk7258_wifi_cpdu cpdu;
1125:   struct bk7258_wifi_event_hdr event;
1126:   uint32_t event_address;
1127:   irqstate_t flags;
1128: 
1129:   flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
1130:   if (generation != bk7258_mailbox_peer_reset_generation() ||
1131:       !wifi_cp_pointer(cpdu_address, sizeof(cpdu)))
1132:     {
1133:       rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1134:       return false;
1135:     }
1136: 
1137:   memcpy(&cpdu, (const void *)(uintptr_t)cpdu_address, sizeof(cpdu));
1138:   event_address = cpdu_address + sizeof(cpdu);
1139:   if (cpdu.length < sizeof(cpdu) + sizeof(event) ||
1140:       !wifi_cp_range(event_address, sizeof(event)))
1141:     {
1142:       rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1143:       return false;
1144:     }
1145: 
1146:   memcpy(&event, (const void *)(uintptr_t)event_address, sizeof(event));
1147:   if (event.length > cpdu.length - sizeof(cpdu) - sizeof(event) ||
1148:       !wifi_cp_range(event_address + WIFI_EVENT_DATA_OFFSET, event.length))
1149:     {
1150:       rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1151:       return false;
1152:     }
1153: 
1154:   *next = cpdu.next;
1155:   rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1156:   return true;
1157: }

1159: static void wifi_handle_command_list(const struct bk7258_wifi_ipc_node *node,
1160:                                      uint32_t generation)
1161: {
1162:   uint32_t addresses[BK7258_WIFI_MAX_LIST];
1163:   uint32_t address = node->head;
1164:   unsigned int count;
1165: 
1166:   if (node->channel != 0 || node->num == 0 ||
1167:       node->num > BK7258_WIFI_MAX_LIST)
1168:     {
1169:       return;
1170:     }
1171: 
1172:   for (count = 0; count < node->num; count++)
1173:     {
1174:       uint32_t next;
1175:       unsigned int previous;
1176: 
1177:       if (!wifi_validate_command(address, &next, generation))
1178:         {
1179:           return;
1180:         }
1181:       for (previous = 0; previous < count; previous++)
1182:         {
1183:           if (addresses[previous] == address)
1184:             {
1185:               return;
1186:             }
1187:         }
1188:       if ((count + 1 == node->num) != (address == node->tail))
1189:         {
1190:           return;
1191:         }
1192: 
1193:       addresses[count] = address;
1194:       address = next;
1195:     }
1196: 
1197:   if (address != 0)
1198:     {
1199:       return;
1200:     }
1201: 
1202:   for (count = 0; count < node->num; count++)
1203:     {
1204:       if (generation != bk7258_mailbox_peer_reset_generation())
1205:         {
1206:           return;
1207:         }
1208: 
1209:       wifi_handle_command(addresses[count], generation);
1210:     }
1211: }

1295: static bool wifi_copy_rx_frame(uint32_t cpdu_address,
1296:                                struct wifi_rx_packet *packet,
1297:                                uint8_t *vif)
1298: {
1299:   struct bk7258_wifi_cpdu cpdu;
1300:   struct bk7258_wifi_pbuf pbuf;
1301:   uint32_t pbuf_address;
1302: 
1303:   if (!wifi_cp_pointer(cpdu_address, sizeof(cpdu)) ||
1304:       cpdu_address < BK7258_CP_RAM_START + sizeof(pbuf))
1305:     {
1306:       return false;
1307:     }
1308: 
1309:   memcpy(&cpdu, (const void *)(uintptr_t)cpdu_address, sizeof(cpdu));
1310:   pbuf_address = cpdu_address - sizeof(pbuf);
1311:   if (!wifi_cp_pointer(pbuf_address, sizeof(pbuf)))
1312:     {
1313:       return false;
1314:     }
1315: 
1316:   memcpy(&pbuf, (const void *)(uintptr_t)pbuf_address, sizeof(pbuf));
1317:   if ((cpdu.flags & 1u) != 0 || pbuf.next != 0 || pbuf.len == 0 ||
1318:       pbuf.len > BK7258_WIFI_MAX_FRAME || pbuf.tot_len != pbuf.len ||
1319:       pbuf.ref == 0 || pbuf.ref == UINT8_MAX ||
1320:       !wifi_cp_pointer(pbuf.payload, pbuf.len))
1321:     {
1322:       return false;
1323:     }
1324: 
1325:   if (packet != NULL)
1326:     {
1327:       memcpy(packet->frame, (const void *)(uintptr_t)pbuf.payload, pbuf.len);
1328:       packet->length = pbuf.len;
1329:     }
1330:   if (vif != NULL)
1331:     {
1332:       *vif = bk7258_wifi_cpdu_get_vif(cpdu.flags);
1333:     }
1334:   return true;
1335: }

1337: static void wifi_recycle_append(struct bk7258_wifi_ipc_node *node,
1338:                                 uint32_t cpdu_address)
1339: {
1340:   struct bk7258_wifi_cpdu *cpdu =
1341:     (struct bk7258_wifi_cpdu *)(uintptr_t)cpdu_address;
1342:   uint32_t pbuf_address;
1343:   struct bk7258_wifi_pbuf *pbuf;
1344: 
1345:   pbuf_address = cpdu_address - sizeof(*pbuf);
1346:   pbuf = (struct bk7258_wifi_pbuf *)(uintptr_t)pbuf_address;
1347: 
1348:   /* Match wdrv_txdata_sender(): CP drops one reference before pbuf_free(). */
1349: 
1350:   pbuf->ref++;
1351:   cpdu->flags |= 1u;
1352:   cpdu->next = 0;
1353:   if (node->tail != 0)
1354:     {
1355:       ((struct bk7258_wifi_cpdu *)(uintptr_t)node->tail)->next =
1356:         cpdu_address;
1357:     }
1358:   else
1359:     {
1360:       node->head = cpdu_address;
1361:     }
1362: 
1363:   node->tail = cpdu_address;
1364:   node->num++;
1365: }

1367: static void wifi_recycle_complete(
1368:   const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *ack, int result, void *arg)
1369: {
1370:   struct wifi_recycle_entry *entry = arg;
1371:   irqstate_t flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
1372: 
1373:   (void)ack;
1374:   if (entry->state == WIFI_RECYCLE_SENDING)
1375:     {
1376:       if (result == OK || entry->generation !=
1377:           bk7258_mailbox_peer_reset_generation())
1378:         {
1379:           entry->state = WIFI_RECYCLE_DISCARD;
1380:         }
1381:       else
1382:         {
1383:           entry->state = WIFI_RECYCLE_QUEUED;
1384:         }
1385:     }
1386: 
1387:   rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1388:   nxsem_post(&g_wifi.work_sem);
1389: }

1391: static void wifi_flush_recycle(void)
1392: {
1393:   struct wifi_recycle_entry *entry;
1394:   irqstate_t flags;
1395:   int ret;
1396: 
1397:   for (;;)
1398:     {
1399:       flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
1400:       if (g_wifi.recycle_count == 0)
1401:         {
1402:           rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1403:           return;
1404:         }
1405: 
1406:       entry = &g_wifi.recycle[g_wifi.recycle_head];
1407:       if (entry->generation != g_wifi.reset_generation)
1408:         {
1409:           entry->state = WIFI_RECYCLE_DISCARD;
1410:         }
1411: 
1412:       if (entry->state == WIFI_RECYCLE_DISCARD)
1413:         {
1414:           memset(entry, 0, sizeof(*entry));
1415:           g_wifi.recycle_head = (g_wifi.recycle_head + 1) %
1416:                                 WIFI_RECYCLE_QUEUE;
1417:           g_wifi.recycle_count--;
1418:           rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1419:           bk7258_mbox_kick_rx();
1420:           continue;
1421:         }
1422: 
1423:       if (entry->state != WIFI_RECYCLE_QUEUED ||
1424:           !bk7258_mailbox_link_ready())
1425:         {
1426:           rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1427:           return;
1428:         }
1429: 
1430:       entry->state = WIFI_RECYCLE_SENDING;
1431:       rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1432:       ret = wifi_send_node_async(BK7258_WIFI_DATA_TX_CHANNEL, &entry->node,
1433:                                  wifi_recycle_complete, entry);
1434:       if (ret < 0)
1435:         {
1436:           flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
1437:           if (entry->state == WIFI_RECYCLE_SENDING)
1438:             {
1439:               entry->state = WIFI_RECYCLE_QUEUED;
1440:             }
1441:           rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1442:         }
1443: 
1444:       return;
1445:     }
1446: }

1448: static void wifi_handle_data(const struct wifi_pending_node *pending,
1449:                              struct wifi_net_notifications *notifications)
1450: {
1451:   const struct bk7258_wifi_ipc_node *node = &pending->node;
1452:   uint32_t addresses[BK7258_WIFI_MAX_LIST];
1453:   bool cp_owned[BK7258_WIFI_MAX_LIST];
1454:   struct wifi_recycle_entry *recycle;
1455:   uint32_t address = node->head;
1456:   uint8_t packet_added = 0;
1457:   unsigned int count;
1458:   irqstate_t flags;
1459: 
1460:   if (!pending->recycle_reserved || node->channel != 2 ||
1461:       node->num == 0 || node->num > BK7258_WIFI_MAX_LIST)
1462:     {
1463:       return;
1464:     }
1465: 
1466:   nxmutex_lock(&g_wifi.packet_lock);
1467:   flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
1468:   recycle = &g_wifi.recycle[pending->recycle_index];
1469:   if (pending->generation != g_wifi.reset_generation ||
1470:       pending->generation != bk7258_mailbox_peer_reset_generation())
1471:     {
1472:       recycle->state = WIFI_RECYCLE_DISCARD;
1473:       rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1474:       nxmutex_unlock(&g_wifi.packet_lock);
1475:       return;
1476:     }
1477:   rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1478: 
1479:   /* First pass validates the complete list without changing either core's
1480:    * ownership.  A malformed list is left untouched.
1481:    */
1482: 
1483:   for (count = 0; count < node->num; count++)
1484:     {
1485:       struct bk7258_wifi_cpdu cpdu;
1486:       struct wifi_tx_slot *tx;
1487:       uint32_t next;
1488:       unsigned int previous;
1489: 
1490:       if (address == 0)
1491:         {
1492:           goto invalid;
1493:         }
1494: 
1495:       for (previous = 0; previous < count; previous++)
1496:         {
1497:           if (addresses[previous] == address)
1498:             {
1499:               goto invalid;
1500:             }
1501:         }
1502: 
1503:       if ((count + 1 == node->num) != (address == node->tail))
1504:         {
1505:           goto invalid;
1506:         }
1507: 
1508:       addresses[count] = address;
1509:       tx = wifi_tx_slot(address);
1510:       if (tx != NULL)
1511:         {
1512:           struct bk7258_wifi_cpdu *ap_cpdu =
1513:             (struct bk7258_wifi_cpdu *)tx->headroom;
1514: 
1515:           if (!tx->active || (ap_cpdu->flags & 1u) == 0 ||
1516:               bk7258_wifi_cpdu_get_vif(ap_cpdu->flags) != tx->vif)
1517:             {
1518:               goto invalid;
1519:             }
1520: 
1521:           /* Completion is accepted by slot address even after role_epoch
1522:            * changes.  A role cannot start while any TX slot is busy, and
1523:            * rejecting a late completion here would leak the retained packet.
1524:            */
1525: 
1526:           cp_owned[count] = false;
1527:           next = ap_cpdu->next;
1528:         }
1529:       else
1530:         {
1531:           flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
1532:           if (pending->generation !=
1533:                 bk7258_mailbox_peer_reset_generation() ||
1534:               !wifi_cp_pointer(address, sizeof(cpdu)) ||
1535:               !wifi_copy_rx_frame(address, NULL, NULL))
1536:             {
1537:               rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1538:               goto invalid;
1539:             }
1540: 
1541:           memcpy(&cpdu, (const void *)(uintptr_t)address, sizeof(cpdu));
1542:           rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1543:           cp_owned[count] = true;
1544:           next = cpdu.next;
1545:         }
1546: 
1547:       address = next;
1548:     }
1549: 
1550:   if (address != 0)
1551:     {
1552:       goto invalid;
1553:     }
1554: 
1555:   for (count = 0; count < node->num; count++)
1556:     {
1557:       if (cp_owned[count] &&
1558:           g_wifi.packet_count + packet_added < WIFI_PACKET_QUEUE)
1559:         {
1560:           unsigned int index = (g_wifi.packet_tail + packet_added) %
1561:                                WIFI_PACKET_QUEUE;
1562:           uint8_t vif;
1563: 
1564:           flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
1565:           if (pending->generation ==
1566:                 bk7258_mailbox_peer_reset_generation() &&
1567:               pending->role_epoch == g_wifi.role_epoch &&
1568:               g_wifi.role_state == WIFI_ROLE_ACTIVE &&
1569:               g_wifi.active_role != WIFI_ROLE_NONE &&
1570:               wifi_copy_rx_frame(addresses[count], &g_wifi.packets[index],
1571:                                  &vif) &&
1572:               vif == wifi_role_vif(g_wifi.active_role))
1573:             {
1574:               g_wifi.packets[index].role_epoch = pending->role_epoch;
1575:               packet_added++;
1576:             }
1577:           rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1578:         }
1579:     }
1580: 
1581:   flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
1582:   if (pending->generation != bk7258_mailbox_peer_reset_generation())
1583:     {
1584:       recycle->state = WIFI_RECYCLE_DISCARD;
1585:       rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1586:       nxmutex_unlock(&g_wifi.packet_lock);
1587:       return;
1588:     }
1589: 
1590:   memset(&recycle->node, 0, sizeof(recycle->node));
1591:   recycle->node.channel = 2;
1592:   for (count = 0; count < node->num; count++)
1593:     {
1594:       if (cp_owned[count] &&
1595:           recycle->node.num < BK7258_WIFI_MAX_LIST)
1596:         {
1597:           wifi_recycle_append(&recycle->node, addresses[count]);
1598:         }
1599:     }
1600: 
1601:   __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
1602:   recycle->state = recycle->node.num == 0 ? WIFI_RECYCLE_DISCARD :
1603:                                             WIFI_RECYCLE_QUEUED;
1604:   g_wifi.packet_tail = (g_wifi.packet_tail + packet_added) %
1605:                        WIFI_PACKET_QUEUE;
1606:   g_wifi.packet_count += packet_added;
1607: 
1608:   for (count = 0; count < node->num; count++)
1609:     {
1610:       if (!cp_owned[count])
1611:         {
1612:           struct wifi_tx_slot *tx = wifi_tx_slot(addresses[count]);
1613: 
1614:           notifications->tx_packets[notifications->tx_count++] = tx->packet;
1615:           tx->packet = NULL;
1616:           tx->active = false;
1617:           tx->transport_rejected = false;
1618:         }
1619:     }
1620:   if (packet_added != 0)
1621:     {
1622:       notifications->rxready = true;
1623:     }
1624:   rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1625:   nxmutex_unlock(&g_wifi.packet_lock);
1626:   nxsem_post(&g_wifi.work_sem);
1627:   return;
1628: 
1629: invalid:
1630:   flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
1631:   recycle->state = WIFI_RECYCLE_DISCARD;
1632:   rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1633:   nxmutex_unlock(&g_wifi.packet_lock);
1634: }

1637: static int wifi_mailbox_rx(const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message,
1638:                            uint8_t *ack_flags, void *arg)
1639: {
1640:   struct bk7258_wifi_ipc_node node;
1641:   struct wifi_pending_node *pending;
1642:   irqstate_t flags;
1643: 
1644:   (void)ack_flags;
1645:   (void)arg;
1646:   memcpy(&node, message, sizeof(node));
1647:   if (node.num == 0 || node.num > BK7258_WIFI_MAX_LIST)
1648:     {
1649:       return -EINVAL;
1650:     }
1651: 
1652:   flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
1653:   if (g_wifi.node_count == WIFI_NODE_QUEUE ||
1654:       (node.channel == 2 &&
1655:        g_wifi.recycle_count == WIFI_RECYCLE_QUEUE))
1656:     {
1657:       rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1658:       return -EAGAIN;
1659:     }
1660: 
1661:   pending = &g_wifi.nodes[g_wifi.node_tail];
1662:   memset(pending, 0, sizeof(*pending));
1663:   pending->node = node;
1664:   pending->generation = bk7258_mailbox_peer_reset_generation();
1665:   pending->role_epoch = g_wifi.role_epoch;
1666:   if (node.channel == 2)
1667:     {
1668:       struct wifi_recycle_entry *entry =
1669:         &g_wifi.recycle[g_wifi.recycle_tail];
1670: 
1671:       memset(entry, 0, sizeof(*entry));
1672:       entry->generation = pending->generation;
1673:       entry->state = WIFI_RECYCLE_RESERVED;
1674:       pending->recycle_index = g_wifi.recycle_tail;
1675:       pending->recycle_reserved = true;
1676:       g_wifi.recycle_tail = (g_wifi.recycle_tail + 1) %
1677:                             WIFI_RECYCLE_QUEUE;
1678:       g_wifi.recycle_count++;
1679:     }
1680: 
1681:   g_wifi.node_tail = (g_wifi.node_tail + 1) % WIFI_NODE_QUEUE;
1682:   g_wifi.node_count++;
1683:   rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
1684:   nxsem_post(&g_wifi.work_sem);
1685:   return OK;
1686: }

1688: static void wifi_link_changed(enum bk7258_mb_link_state state, void *arg)

1: # Wi-Fi 使用说明
2: 
3: 当前固件使用单个 `wlan0`，STA 和 SoftAP 模式互斥运行。连接开发板 UART0 后，
4: 在 CP 控制台执行 `ap_console open` 进入 NSH。
5: 
6: ## STA 模式
7: 
8: 连接 2.4 GHz 热点：
9: 
10: ```sh
11: ifup wlan0
12: wapi scan wlan0                    # 看有哪些热点；encode=8000 是开放网络
13: wapi psk wlan0 <密码> 3            # 开放热点跳过这行
14: wapi essid wlan0 <2.4G_SSID> 1
15: renew wlan0                        # 失败就再来一次，见下
16: ifconfig wlan0
17: ```
18: 
19: `renew wlan0` 用于通过 DHCP 获取热点分配的 IP、掩码和默认网关，不能省略。
20: 
21: **首次 `renew` 可能失败。** 关联完成到能收发 DHCP 之间有一段窗口，实测第一次报
22: `ERROR: netlib_obtain_ipv4addr() failed`、第二次成功。重试一次再判断。
23: 
24: ### 怎么判断真的通了
25: 
26: 看 `ifconfig wlan0` 两件事：状态是 `RUNNING`（不是 `UP` 也不是 `DOWN`），以及地址
27: 不再是 `10.0.0.2`——那个是 NuttX 的默认静态地址，没配网时就长这样。
28: 
29: ```
30: wlan0	Link encap:Ethernet HWaddr c8:47:8c:55:6b:ea at RUNNING mtu 1500
31: 	inet addr:10.192.105.127 DRaddr:10.192.104.1 Mask:255.255.254.0
32: ```
33: 
34: **不要用 `ping` 当判据。** 实测环境屏蔽 ICMP：`ping 8.8.8.8` 与
35: `ping <解析出的 IP>` 都 100% 丢包，而同一时刻 DNS 和 TLS 都是通的。用下面两个之一：
36: 
37: ```sh
38: ping -c 2 www.baidu.com    # 只看它是否打印出解析到的 IP，即 DNS 通了；丢包可以忽略
39: ```
40: 
41: 或者进 agent 跑一次真实的 HTTPS：
42: 
43: ```
44: ai_agent
45: net_test
46: ```
47: 
48: 期望输出：
49: 
50: ```
51: [vela_tls] Handshake OK: TLSv1.2 / TLS-DHE-RSA-WITH-AES-256-CBC-SHA
52: SUCCESS! HTTP Status: 200
53: ```
54: 
55: `net_status` 的 `Network connected: yes` **不能**作为判据：它只检查有没有配上地址，
56: 接口 DOWN 时也会这么说。
57: 
58: ## SoftAP 模式
59: 
60: 以下配置已在 BK7258 实板验证手机可发现并连接热点：
61: 
62: ```sh
63: ifdown wlan0
64: ifup wlan0
65: wapi mode wlan0 3
66: wapi freq wlan0 6 1
67: wapi psk wlan0 12345678 3
68: wapi essid wlan0 VelaSight_AP 1
69: dhcpd_start wlan0
70: ```
71: 
72: 其中：
73: 
74: - `3` 表示 `WAPI_MODE_MASTER` 或 WPA-CCMP。
75: - channel 固定为 6，可按现场 2.4 GHz 信道占用改为 1 至 13。
76: - WPA2 密码必须为 8 至 63 字节。
77: - `dhcpd_start` 会将板端配置为 `192.168.10.1/24`。
78: - DHCP 地址池为 `192.168.10.2` 起，最多分配 4 个租约。
79: 
80: 检查运行状态：
81: 
82: ```sh
83: ifconfig wlan0
84: wapi show wlan0
85: ```
86: 
87: 成功时 `ifconfig` 必须显示 `RUNNING`，`wapi show` 应显示
88: `WAPI_MODE_MASTER`、目标 ESSID、channel 和 AP MAC。只有 `UP` 而没有
89: `RUNNING` 表示配置已保存，但 CP 尚未成功启动 beacon。
90: 
91: 手机连接：
92: 
93: ```text
94: SSID: VelaSight_AP
95: 密码: 12345678
96: IP 设置: DHCP/自动
97: ```
98: 
99: 停止 SoftAP：
100: 
101: ```sh
102: dhcpd_stop
103: ifdown wlan0
104: ```
105: 
106: 切回 STA：
107: 
108: ```sh
109: ifup wlan0
110: wapi mode wlan0 2
111: wapi psk wlan0 <路由器密码> 3
112: wapi essid wlan0 <2.4G_SSID> 1
113: renew wlan0
114: ifconfig wlan0
115: ```
116: 
117: ## 故障排查
118: 
119: - `dhcpd_start: command not found`：当前 AP 分区不是启用 SoftAP DHCP 的最新
120:   `nsh` 镜像。`help` 的 `Builtin Apps` 必须包含 `dhcpd_start` 和 `dhcpd_stop`。
121: - 手机扫描不到热点：先检查 `ifconfig wlan0` 是否为 `RUNNING`；`wapi show`
122:   只能证明配置已保存，不能单独证明热点已经发 beacon。
123: - 重复启动 DHCP 前先执行 `dhcpd_stop`，避免旧服务仍占用 UDP 端口 67。
124: - SoftAP 模式不支持与 STA 并发；切换角色前必须停止当前角色。
125: 
126: ## 注意
127: 
128: - 不要把真实 Wi-Fi 密码提交到仓库或测试日志中。开放热点不涉及这个问题。
129: - 示例 SoftAP 密码仅用于开发测试，产品使用时必须替换。
130: - 当前的 HTTPS 是加密但未验证证书的（无 RTC/SNTP，且 `VERIFY_OPTIONAL`），详见
131:   `docs/8.16基础适配门禁验收记录.md` 第 7 节。

233:  * Name: bk7258_report_cache
234:  *
235:  * Description:
236:  *   Reports whether this core implements instruction and data caches, and is
237:  *   left in at boot so the next person does not have to guess.
238:  *
239:  *   The AP executes in place from flash at 0x02150000.  NuttX did not enable
240:  *   the instruction cache until commit "perf(bk7258): enable the AP
241:  *   instruction cache", and every instruction fetch was a flash access: the
242:  *   expression renderer cost ~455ms per frame for work that takes 0.09ms on a
243:  *   host, a 51200-byte word-at-a-time copy ran at 0.8MB/s, and raising the
244:  *   core to 480MHz changed none of it because the core was never the limit.
245:  *   The same frame now costs 37ms.
246:  *
247:  *   Turning it on needed two independent fixes, and the first one alone looks
248:  *   like "the cache does nothing": CONFIG_ARMV8M_ICACHE depends on the hidden
249:  *   ARMV8M_HAVE_ICACHE, which this chip's Kconfig did not select, so asking
250:  *   for it in a defconfig was silently dropped; and selecting it only compiles
251:  *   up_enable_icache() in -- every other ARMv8-M chip in the tree calls that
252:  *   from its own start code, this one did not.  Both are fixed now (see the
253:  *   chip Kconfig and bk7258_start.c).
254:  *
255:  *   Only the I-Cache is on.  Instruction fetch is read-only and needs no
256:  *   maintenance against the camera, panel and mailbox DMA that shares AP RAM,
257:  *   which the MPU deliberately keeps non-cacheable.
258:  *
259:  *   CLIDR/CTR exist in ARMv8-M whether or not a cache is fitted (they read
260:  *   zero when it is not), so reading them is safe and settles the question:
261:  *   this part reports CLIDR=0x09200003, i.e. both caches are implemented.
262:  *
263:  ****************************************************************************/

68:  * @brief
69:  *   The core event loop and main logic of the DHCP server daemon.

**Scope Summary**

The repository contains two materially different BK7258 images:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/out/beken_bk7258-ap_nsh/.config`: networking and Wi-Fi are disabled. This image cannot perform STA or SoftAP operation.
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_ai_agent/.config`: Wi-Fi, WAPI, IPv4, DHCP client/server, and the BK7258 Wi-Fi IPC driver are enabled. This is the relevant configuration for app-callable STA/AP control.

The primary implementation is under:

- [/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_wifi.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_wifi.c)
- [/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/include/bk7258_wifi.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/include/bk7258_wifi.h)
- [/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/apps/include/wireless/wapi.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/apps/include/wireless/wapi.h)
- [/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/apps/include/netutils/dhcpd.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/apps/include/netutils/dhcpd.h)

There is also a project copy under:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/...`

The vendor tree is the source path used by the active build output and should be treated as the implementation reference unless the project build scripts explicitly override it.

## 1. BK7258 Button Mappings

### GPIO mappings

[/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/include/board.h:15-26](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/include/board.h:15) defines:

```c
#define BOARD_KEY_VOLUME_UP_GPIO   13
#define BOARD_KEY_POWER_GPIO       12
#define BOARD_KEY_VOLUME_DOWN_GPIO 8

#define BUTTON_VOLUME_UP           0
#define BUTTON_POWER               1
#define BUTTON_VOLUME_DOWN         2

#define NUM_BUTTONS                3

#define BUTTON_VOLUME_UP_BIT       (1u << BUTTON_VOLUME_UP)
#define BUTTON_POWER_BIT           (1u << BUTTON_POWER)
#define BUTTON_VOLUME_DOWN_BIT     (1u << BUTTON_VOLUME_DOWN)
```

The resulting bit mapping is:

| Logical button | GPIO | Bit |
|---|---:|---:|
| Volume up | GPIO13 | `1u << 0` |
| Power | GPIO12 | `1u << 1` |
| Volume down | GPIO8 | `1u << 2` |

The buttons are active-low. [/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_buttons.c:60-62](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_buttons.c:60) configures each GPIO with an internal pull-up. A pressed button is detected when the GPIO reads low.

### Board-level polling APIs

[/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/include/board.h:40-43](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/include/board.h:40) declares:

```c
uint32_t board_button_initialize(void);
```

Implementation:

```c
uint32_t board_button_initialize(void);
```

Defined at [/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_buttons.c:56-72](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_buttons.c:56).

Behavior:

- Configures GPIO13, GPIO12, and GPIO8 as pull-up inputs.
- If `CONFIG_DEV_GPIO` is enabled, registers one GPIO input device per button using `gpio_pin_register()`.
- Returns `NUM_BUTTONS`, currently `3`.

The board-level current-state API is defined in the C file but not declared in `board.h`:

```c
uint32_t board_buttons(void);
```

Defined at [/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_buttons.c:74-88](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_buttons.c:74).

It returns an active-high bitmask:

```c
uint32_t pressed = board_buttons();

if ((pressed & BUTTON_POWER_BIT) != 0)
  {
    /* GPIO12 power key is pressed */
  }
```

The implementation reads:

```c
if (!bk7258_gpio_read(g_button_pins[i]))
  {
    pressed |= 1u << i;
  }
```

There is no debounce in `board_buttons()` itself.

### GPIO device registration

When `CONFIG_DEV_GPIO` is enabled, each button gets a GPIO device structure with:

```c
static int bk7258_button_read(struct gpio_dev_s *dev, bool *value);
```

The read callback returns active-high logical state:

```c
*value = !bk7258_gpio_read(g_button_pins[button->id]);
```

Relevant code:

- [/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_buttons.c:15-21](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_buttons.c:15)
- [/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_buttons.c:33-52](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_buttons.c:33)

The registrations use numeric pin IDs `0`, `1`, and `2`:

```c
gpio_pin_register(&g_button_gpio[i].gpio, i);
```

This is not the generic NuttX `/dev/btnN` upper-half interface. The board code does not call `btn_register()`, and no button interrupt lower-half is implemented.

The generic button API exists at:

[/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/include/nuttx/input/buttons.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/include/nuttx/input/buttons.h)

It supports:

```c
int btn_register(FAR const char *devname,
                 FAR const struct btn_lowerhalf_s *lower);
```

and ioctl-based event delivery through:

```c
#define BTNIOC_SUPPORTED
#define BTNIOC_POLLEVENTS
#define BTNIOC_REGISTER
```

However, the BK7258 board implementation does not currently use this API. An application should therefore use `board_buttons()` through a small board-facing wrapper, or consume the registered GPIO devices if the intended GPIO device path and API are confirmed for the target image.

### Kconfig prerequisites for buttons

Board selection:

[/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/Kconfig:3-7](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/Kconfig:3)

```kconfig
config ARCH_BOARD_BK7258_AP
    bool "BK7258 AP board"
    default y
    select ARCH_HAVE_BUTTONS
    select ARCH_HAVE_LEDS
```

Common board options in the active image include:

```text
CONFIG_ARCH_HAVE_BUTTONS=y
CONFIG_ARCH_BUTTONS=y
CONFIG_DEV_GPIO=y
```

The current `ap_nsh` image confirms:

[/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/out/beken_bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:324-333](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/out/beken_bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:324)

```text
# CONFIG_BOARD_CUSTOM_BUTTONS is not set
CONFIG_ARCH_HAVE_BUTTONS=y
CONFIG_ARCH_BUTTONS=y
```

Despite `CONFIG_BOARD_CUSTOM_BUTTONS` being unset, the custom board source directly supplies `board_button_initialize()` and `board_buttons()`.

For the GPIO registration path:

```text
CONFIG_DEV_GPIO=y
```

is required. The board code itself can still read buttons through `board_buttons()` without the GPIO upper-half registration.

## 2. Debounce Implementation

The only BK7258 debounce implementation found is the power-key motor worker:

[/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_motor.c:25-27](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_motor.c:25)

```c
#define BK7258_KEY_POLL_US        5000
#define BK7258_KEY_DEBOUNCE_COUNT 6
```

The worker samples every 5 ms:

```c
bool sample = (board_buttons() & BUTTON_POWER_BIT) != 0;
```

It requires six consecutive equal samples before accepting a state transition:

```c
if (sample != candidate)
  {
    candidate = sample;
    samples = 1;
  }
else if (samples < BK7258_KEY_DEBOUNCE_COUNT)
  {
    samples++;
  }

if (samples == BK7258_KEY_DEBOUNCE_COUNT && pressed != candidate)
  {
    ...
    pressed = candidate;
  }
```

This gives approximately a 30 ms debounce qualification period:

```text
5 ms sample interval * 6 samples = 30 ms
```

The worker signature is:

```c
static int bk7258_motor_button_worker(int argc, char **argv);
```

It is created by:

```c
int bk7258_power_key_motor_start(void);
```

using:

```c
pid = kthread_create("power-key-motor", 100, 1536,
                     bk7258_motor_button_worker, NULL);
```

Important characteristics:

- It debounces only the power key.
- It is a polling debounce algorithm, not interrupt-based.
- It drives `/dev/pwm0` while the power key remains pressed.
- The worker runs indefinitely.
- There is no public stop API for this worker.
- `bk7258_power_key_motor_start()` has no idempotence guard of its own. `bk7258_bringup()` normally calls it once.

Kconfig:

[/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/Kconfig:31-38](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/Kconfig:31)

```kconfig
config BK7258_POWER_KEY_MOTOR
    bool "Vibrate while the power key is pressed"
    default n
    depends on ARCH_BUTTONS && PWM
```

The active AI-agent build enables:

```text
CONFIG_ARCH_BUTTONS=y
CONFIG_PWM=y
CONFIG_BK7258_POWER_KEY_MOTOR=y
```

A reusable application button service should copy the same sampling model, but should avoid directly depending on the motor worker’s private static constants. Recommended parameters are:

```c
#define BK7258_BUTTON_POLL_US        5000
#define BK7258_BUTTON_DEBOUNCE_COUNT 6
```

Hazards:

- `board_buttons()` is an instantaneous raw state read.
- Calling it directly from an app can produce multiple transitions due to contact bounce.
- There is no event queue or edge timestamping.
- `board_button_initialize()` must run before reads.
- The power-key worker already samples GPIO12. A second consumer is technically possible because reads are passive, but both consumers must agree on debounce semantics.
- Avoid doing Wi-Fi switching directly from a polling loop. Post a debounced event to a control worker.

## 3. BK7258 Wi-Fi Driver and App-Callable Surface

### Low-level initialization

Public declaration:

[/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/include/bk7258_wifi.h:8](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/include/bk7258_wifi.h:8)

```c
int bk7258_wifi_initialize(void);
```

Implementation:

[/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_wifi.c:2656-2767](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_wifi.c:2656)

Initialization does the following:

- Initializes command, packet, scan, and role synchronization primitives.
- Registers mailbox RX handlers.
- Starts the `bk-wifi` worker thread.
- Queries the Wi-Fi MAC address.
- Queries AP status.
- Queries WLAN status.
- Registers the lower-half network device.
- Installs the wireless operation table.
- Defaults the configured role to STA.
- Registers `wlan0` through `netdev_lower_register()`.

The board bring-up calls it conditionally:

[/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:174-180](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:174)

```c
#ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_WIFI
  ret = bk7258_wifi_initialize();
  if (ret < 0)
    {
      return ret;
    }
#endif
```

This is an initialization API, not a complete STA/AP management API. Applications should use the standard WAPI functions after board bring-up has registered `wlan0`.

### Wi-Fi IPC commands

The BK7258 controller ABI is defined at:

[/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/hardware/bk7258_wifi_ipc.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/hardware/bk7258_wifi_ipc.h)

Relevant command IDs:

```c
#define BK7258_WIFI_CMD_SCAN_WIFI             1u
#define BK7258_WIFI_CMD_CONNECT               2u
#define BK7258_WIFI_CMD_DISCONNECT            3u
#define BK7258_WIFI_CMD_GET_WLAN_STATUS       7u
#define BK7258_WIFI_CMD_GET_MAC_ADDR          0x202u
#define BK7258_WIFI_CMD_OPENVELA_SCAN_PAGE    0x20du
#define BK7258_WIFI_CMD_OPENVELA_COUNTRY_GET  0x20eu
#define BK7258_WIFI_CMD_OPENVELA_COUNTRY_SET  0x20fu

Internal API:

```c

It:

- Returns `OK` if no role is active.
- Returns `-EBUSY` if already stopping.
- Marks the role as `WIFI_ROLE_STOPPING`.
- Disables carrier and TX.
- Sends `BK7258_WIFI_CMD_DISCONNECT` for STA.
- Sends `BK7258_WIFI_CMD_OPENVELA_AP_STOP` for SoftAP.
- Waits for the relevant event.
- Uses a 3-second role stop timeout.
- Queries STA status after a STA timeout as a fallback.
- Restores prior state on non-timeout errors when possible.

## 8. Configuration and Service Lifecycle Patterns

### Board bring-up sequencing

[/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:115-229](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:115)

The bring-up sequence is:

1. Initialize buttons.
2. Mount procfs if enabled.
3. Set up PWM.
4. Wait for mailbox link.
5. Start IPC heartbeat.
6. Start PWC.
7. Schedule SD-NAND initialization if enabled.
8. Initialize Wi-Fi if `CONFIG_BK7258_WIFI`.
9. Initialize optional TRNG/media.
10. Start the power-key motor worker.

The Wi-Fi service depends on the mailbox link being ready first.

Hazard:

- Applications should not call Wi-Fi configuration before `bk7258_wifi_initialize()` and network device registration have completed.
- The board bring-up returns early on several failures. An app-facing service should expose a clear “radio ready” state rather than assuming boot completion means `wlan0` is usable.

### DHCPD lifecycle pattern

The DHCPD service uses:

```text
global state
task_create()
signal-driven stop
waitpid() for synchronous teardown
```

This is appropriate for a single global server but not for multiple independently managed services.

The AI-agent sources contain useful lifecycle patterns:

```c
int heartbeat_init(void);
int heartbeat_start(void);
void heartbeat_stop(void);
```

It uses an atomic-style running flag and lets the thread exit on its next loop. This is simple but stop is asynchronous.

Node client:

[/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/packages/ai_agent/src/node/node_client.c:773-850](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/packages/ai_agent/src/node/node_client.c:773)

```c
int node_client_init(void);
int node_client_start(void);
void node_client_stop(void);
```

This is a stronger lifecycle pattern:

1. Set the running flag false.
2. Shutdown/close the blocking file descriptor.
3. Join the worker thread.
4. Free TLS/resources only after the worker exits.
5. Support restart by stopping an existing instance first.

This model is preferable for Wi-Fi orchestration because Wi-Fi stop operations can block while waiting for controller events.

Network manager:

[/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/packages/ai_agent/src/infra/network_manager.c:629-694](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/packages/ai_agent/src/infra/network_manager.c:629)

uses:

```c
pthread_create()
pthread_attr_setstacksize()
pthread_attr_destroy()
```

and maintains a dedicated poll thread. It does not provide a complete stop path in the inspected section, so it is less suitable as a lifecycle template than `node_client.c`.

### Recommended lifecycle rule

Use one serialized network-control worker with:

```text
init -> start -> request transition -> wait for state -> stop -> join/destroy
```

Do not let multiple callers invoke WAPI and DHCP APIs concurrently.

## 9. Hazards and Failure Cases

### Current image mismatch

The biggest operational hazard is confusing the two images.

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/out/beken_bk7258-ap_nsh/.config` has:

```text
# CONFIG_NET is not set
# CONFIG_DRIVERS_WIRELESS is not set
```

The AI-agent image has Wi-Fi enabled. Test the exact output image, not merely the source tree or object files.

### Mode changes while active

`wifi_mode()` returns `-EBUSY` if a role is active.

Correct sequence:

```text
dhcpd_stop()                  /* if AP DHCP is running */
wapi_set_ifdown()
wapi_set_mode(... desired role ...)
configure SSID/auth/channel
wapi_set_ifup()
wapi_connect/start role
```

Do not call `wapi_set_mode()` first and expect it to stop the current role.

### `ifup` is not necessarily role start

The driver’s `wifi_ifup()` only marks `admin_up`. The actual role starts through the wireless handler’s connect operation after mode and credentials are configured.

The app should therefore model these as separate states:

```text
ADMIN_DOWN
ADMIN_UP_CONFIGURED
ROLE_STARTING
ROLE_ACTIVE
```

### DHCP service ordering

For AP:

```text
set AP IP/netmask
dhcpd_start("wlan0")
```

For leaving AP:

```text
dhcpd_stop()
wapi_set_ifdown()
```

Do not leave DHCPD bound to `wlan0` while switching the interface into STA mode.

### STA DHCP timing

The repository documents that the first STA DHCP attempt can fail because association and usable packet transport are not synchronized. Retry `netlib_obtain_ipv4addr("wlan0")` after a short delay, with a bounded retry count.

### Carrier and IP are different

The driver tracks carrier separately from administrative state. The project warns that an interface can have an address while not actually being `RUNNING`.

Use both:

- interface operational/carrier state
- assigned address

Do not use only “has an IP” as the connected condition.

### AP status is asynchronous

AP start sends an IPC command, then queries AP status and processes start events. A successful command transport result is not by itself proof that beacons are active.

The driver explicitly checks:

```c
ap_status.started
```

and returns `-EIO` if the controller reports that AP did not start.

### No STA/AP concurrency

The driver has separate wire VIF identifiers, but the role state machine permits only one active role. Do not infer concurrent STA+AP support from the presence of two VIF constants.

### WAPI abstraction mismatch

WAPI is generic, but the BK7258 driver supports a narrow subset:

- STA: `IW_MODE_INFRA`
- AP: `IW_MODE_MASTER`
- WPA: disabled or WPA2
- Cipher: none or CCMP
- AP channel: 1 through 14

Unsupported generic WAPI modes may return `-EINVAL` or `-EOPNOTSUPP`.

### Button API is not event-driven

The board exposes raw polling and GPIO registration, but no `/dev/btnN` event device is registered. An app requiring short-press/long-press semantics must add its own debouncer and event worker.

### Long-running workers

The power-key motor worker and Wi-Fi worker run indefinitely. There is no general service manager that owns or joins all board workers. Any new orchestration worker should:

- have a stop flag or control semaphore
- avoid blocking forever on a controller operation
- use explicit join or completion signaling
- avoid destroying shared state until worker exit

## 10. Recommended Minimal STA/AP Orchestration Interface

The repository does not currently expose one cohesive public `bk7258_wifi_set_mode()` API for applications. The minimal practical interface should be a new app-facing wrapper built on existing WAPI, netlib, and DHCPD APIs.

Suggested public header:

```c
#ifndef BK7258_WIFI_ORCHESTRATOR_H
#define BK7258_WIFI_ORCHESTRATOR_H

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>

enum bk7258_wifi_role_e
{
  BK7258_WIFI_ROLE_NONE = 0,
  BK7258_WIFI_ROLE_STA,
  BK7258_WIFI_ROLE_SOFTAP
};

enum bk7258_wifi_state_e
{
  BK7258_WIFI_STATE_DOWN = 0,
  BK7258_WIFI_STATE_STARTING,
  BK7258_WIFI_STATE_STA_CONNECTED,
  BK7258_WIFI_STATE_AP_ACTIVE,
  BK7258_WIFI_STATE_STOPPING,
  BK7258_WIFI_STATE_ERROR
};

struct bk7258_wifi_sta_config_s
{
  const char *ssid;
  const char *password;
};

struct bk7258_wifi_ap_config_s
{
  const char *ssid;
  const char *password;
  uint8_t channel;
  bool open;
};

struct bk7258_wifi_status_s
{
  enum bk7258_wifi_role_e role;
  enum bk7258_wifi_state_e state;
  bool admin_up;
  bool carrier;
  bool dhcp_ready;
  uint8_t ap_client_count;
};

int bk7258_wifi_orch_init(void);

int bk7258_wifi_orch_start_sta(
  const struct bk7258_wifi_sta_config_s *config);

int bk7258_wifi_orch_start_softap(
  const struct bk7258_wifi_ap_config_s *config);

int bk7258_wifi_orch_stop(void);

int bk7258_wifi_orch_get_status(
  struct bk7258_wifi_status_s *status);

void bk7258_wifi_orch_set_event_callback(
  void (*callback)(const struct bk7258_wifi_status_s *status,
                   void *arg),
  void *arg);

#endif
```

Recommended internal behavior:

### `bk7258_wifi_orch_init()`

- Verify Wi-Fi initialization completed.
- Create the serialized control worker.
- Open one WAPI socket.
- Initialize status to `DOWN`.
- Ensure the callback and status state are protected by a mutex.

### `bk7258_wifi_orch_start_sta()`

1. Validate SSID/password lengths.
2. Stop SoftAP if active.
3. Call `dhcpd_stop()` if AP DHCP is running.
4. Call `wapi_set_ifdown()`.
5. Call:

```c
wapi_set_mode(sock, "wlan0", WAPI_MODE_MANAGED);
```

6. Configure authentication/password.
7. Configure SSID:

```c
wapi_set_essid(sock, "wlan0", ssid, WAPI_ESSID_ON);
```

8. Call:

```c
wapi_set_ifup(sock, "wlan0");
```

9. Initiate the STA connection using the WAPI implementation’s connect/renew path.
10. Wait for carrier/connected state.
11. Call:

```c
netlib_obtain_ipv4addr("wlan0");
```

12. Retry DHCP once or twice with bounded delays.
13. Report `BK7258_WIFI_STATE_STA_CONNECTED` only after carrier and address validation.

### `bk7258_wifi_orch_start_softap()`

1. Validate:
   - SSID nonempty and at most 32 bytes.
   - Channel 1 through 14.
   - Open AP has no password.
   - WPA2 password 8 through 63 bytes.
2. Stop STA if active.
3. Call `wapi_set_ifdown()`.
4. Call:

```c
wapi_set_mode(sock, "wlan0", WAPI_MODE_MASTER);
```

5. Configure channel with the local WAPI frequency helper.
6. Configure WPA2/CCMP or open security.
7. Configure SSID.
8. Set the AP interface address and netmask to match the DHCPD configuration.
9. Call:

```c
wapi_set_ifup(sock, "wlan0");
```

10. Start the role via the WAPI/wireless connect operation.
11. Verify AP status/carrier.
12. Call:

```c
dhcpd_start("wlan0");
```

13. Report `BK7258_WIFI_STATE_AP_ACTIVE`.

### `bk7258_wifi_orch_stop()`

1. Serialize against any start request.
2. Stop DHCPD first if AP is active.
3. Stop the wireless role through WAPI disconnect/ifdown.
4. Wait for role termination.
5. Close or retain the WAPI socket according to orchestrator lifetime.
6. Report `DOWN`.

### Why this interface is minimal

It keeps the existing responsibilities separated:

- BK7258 driver: radio role and controller IPC.
- WAPI: app-callable wireless ioctl configuration.
- `netlib_obtain_ipv4addr()`: STA DHCP.
- `dhcpd_start()/dhcpd_stop()`: SoftAP DHCP lifecycle.
- Orchestrator: ordering, serialization, retries, and state reporting.

It avoids shelling out to:

```text
ifup
ifdown
wapi
renew
dhcpd_start
dhcpd_stop
```

while preserving the same behavior as the documented shell workflow.

## 11. Minimum Kconfig Set for the Recommended Interface

At minimum, the target image needs:

```text
CONFIG_NET=y
CONFIG_NETDEV_IOCTL=y
CONFIG_NETDEV_WIRELESS_IOCTL=y
CONFIG_NETDEV_WIRELESS_HANDLER=y

CONFIG_BK7258_WIFI=y
CONFIG_DRIVERS_WIRELESS=y
CONFIG_DRIVERS_IEEE80211=y

CONFIG_WIRELESS_WAPI=y

CONFIG_NET_IPv4=y
CONFIG_NET_UDP=y
CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPC=y

CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPD=y
CONFIG_SCHED_WAITPID=y
CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPD_SIGWAKEUP=22
```

For the board button path:

```text
CONFIG_ARCH_HAVE_BUTTONS=y
CONFIG_ARCH_BUTTONS=y
CONFIG_DEV_GPIO=y
```

For the existing power-key motor/debounce example:

```text
CONFIG_PWM=y
CONFIG_BK7258_POWER_KEY_MOTOR=y
```

`CONFIG_BK7258_POWER_KEY_MOTOR` is unrelated to Wi-Fi orchestration and should not be required by the new interface.

The direct app-facing implementation should include:

```c
#include <wireless/wapi.h>
#include <netutils/netlib.h>
#include <netutils/dhcpd.h>
```

and should use `board_buttons()` only through a board-specific button adapter if button-triggered mode switching is required.
